title: Completeness characterization of locally presentable categories
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ and use ordinary categories with $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets. All smallness below is relative to $\mathcal U$; object collections may belong to a larger universe. For an infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$, a category is $\kappa$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms has a cocone. Regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$ has size less than $\kappa$. An object $P$ is $\kappa$-presentable if $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. A category is accessible if, for some such $\kappa$, it has all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits and a small family of $\kappa$-presentable objects such that every object is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of that family. Colimits mean [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

Call a category locally presentable if it is accessible and has all small colimits. Call it complete if every small diagram $D:J\to\mathcal A$ admits a limiting cone: an object $L$ with compatible maps $p_j:L\to D(j)$ through which every cone factors uniquely. Call it cocomplete if it has all small colimits. For every category $\mathcal A$ the following three conditions are equivalent: $\mathcal A$ is accessible and complete; $\mathcal A$ is accessible and cocomplete; $\mathcal A$ is locally presentable.

source.place: Agent-formulated categorical input to paragraph 2; Ching--Riehl, Coalgebraic models for combinatorial model categories, Appendix A, Theorem A.2 (Adamek--Rosicky 2.47), printed p. 9. Read online at https://math.jhu.edu/~eriehl/coalgebraic.pdf; not archived. No Stacks tag states this categorical theorem.

external.place: Appendix A, Theorem A.2 (Adamek--Rosicky 2.47), printed p. 9.

proof.text: By the definitions in the statement, accessible and cocomplete means exactly locally presentable. It remains to prove, for accessible $\mathcal A$, that completeness implies cocompleteness and conversely. All the constructions below use only $\mathcal U$-small indexing categories and sets; the objects of $\mathcal A$ need not form a small set.

source.place: Agent proof of the categorical input: logical reduction of Ching--Riehl Theorem A.2 (the cited paper states the result without its proof).

proof.text: Assume $\mathcal A$ accessible and complete, and fix any small $D:J\to\mathcal A$. The product $\mathcal B=\prod_{j\in\operatorname{Ob}J}\mathcal A$ is accessible by [lem-coef-accessible-pie-closure]. Apply [lem-coef-constant-diagonal-accessibility] with $V=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$ at an accessibility cardinal $\kappa$ of $\mathcal A$: the constant functor $F(X)=(D(j))_j$ and diagonal $G(X)=(X)_j$ preserve small $\kappa$-filtered colimits, so are accessible.

source.place: Agent proof, complete implies cocomplete: accessible cocones from the small-product, inserter and equifier clauses of the sibling categorical input (Ching--Riehl Appendix A, Definition A.3 and the preceding paragraph).

proof.text: The inserter $\mathcal I=\operatorname{Ins}(F,G)$ is accessible, and its projection $V:\mathcal I\to\mathcal A$ is accessible, by the product/inserter clause of [lem-coef-accessible-pie-closure]. By [def-coef-inserter], its objects are $(X,(u_j:D(j)\to X)_j)$ and its arrows are maps $h$ satisfying $h u_j=u'_j$.

source.place: Agent proof, complete implies cocomplete: accessible cocones from the small-product, inserter and equifier clauses of the sibling categorical input (Ching--Riehl Appendix A, Definition A.3 and the preceding paragraph).

proof.text:
Choose a regular cardinal $\lambda$ at least the accessibility cardinal of $\mathcal A$ and a preservation cardinal $
u$ for $V$. By the definition of accessible functor, $\mathcal I$ has the required small $
u$-filtered colimits. Every $\lambda$-filtered diagram is $
u$-filtered, so its colimit exists in $\mathcal I$ and $V$ preserves it; its image has a colimit in $\mathcal A$ since it is also filtered at the original cardinal.

source.place: Agent proof, complete implies cocomplete: accessible cocones from the small-product, inserter and equifier clauses of the sibling categorical input (Ching--Riehl Appendix A, Definition A.3 and the preceding paragraph).

proof.text: The product $\mathcal B'=\prod_{a\in\operatorname{Mor}J}\mathcal A$ is accessible by [lem-coef-accessible-pie-closure]. Apply [lem-coef-constant-diagonal-accessibility] with source $\mathcal I$, target $\mathcal A$, $S=\operatorname{Mor}J$, and the colimit-preserving $V$ of Step 4. Thus $H(X,u)=(D(\operatorname{dom}a))_a$ and $K(X,u)=(X)_a$ preserve small $\lambda$-filtered colimits and are accessible.

source.place: Agent proof, complete implies cocomplete: accessible cocones from the small-product, inserter and equifier clauses of the sibling categorical input (Ching--Riehl Appendix A, Definition A.3 and the preceding paragraph).

proof.text: The natural transformations $\alpha,\beta:H\Rightarrow K$ with $\alpha_a=u_{\operatorname{cod}a}D(a)$ and $\beta_a=u_{\operatorname{dom}a}$ have an equifier which is precisely $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Cocone}(D)$, by [lem-coef-cocone-pie-realization]. The equifier clause of [lem-coef-accessible-pie-closure] makes it accessible. This identification also covers the empty diagram $J$.

source.place: Agent proof, complete implies cocomplete: accessible cocones from the small-product, inserter and equifier clauses of the sibling categorical input (Ching--Riehl Appendix A, Definition A.3 and the preceding paragraph).

proof.text: The category $\mathcal E$ is locally small: each of its Hom sets is a subset of a Hom set of $\mathcal A$. It is complete. Given a small diagram $(X_k,u^k)$ of cocones, let $L$ be the limit of its vertices in $\mathcal A$, with projections $p_k$. For each $j$, the compatible arrows $u_j^k:D(j)\to X_k$ uniquely define $u_j:D(j)\to L$. The equations $u_{\operatorname{cod}a}D(a)=u_{\operatorname{dom}a}$ follow after every $p_k$ and therefore by uniqueness into $L$. A cone of cocones factors uniquely through $(L,u)$ by the same vertex-limit property. This works also for an empty diagram of cocones, since the terminal object of $\mathcal A$ has unique arrows from all $D(j)$.

source.place: Agent proof, complete implies cocomplete: limit cones of cocones constructed from their vertices.

proof.text: Choose a small family $(B_s)_{s\in S}$ of presentable generators for the accessible category $\mathcal E$ of Step 6. Every cocone $X$ is a filtered colimit of this family, and the filtered index is nonempty, so at least one of its structure arrows is a map $B_s\to X$. Thus this family is weakly initial. By Step 7 its product $T=\prod_{s\in S}B_s$ exists. For each $X$ choose such an $s$ and compose the projection $T\to B_s$ with $B_s\to X$; this makes $T$ weakly initial. There is no empty-family difficulty: Step 7 supplies a terminal cocone, and a presentation of that object forces $S$ to be nonempty.

source.place: Agent proof, complete implies cocomplete: a small family of accessible generators gives a weakly initial object by taking its product.

proof.text: By Step 7, $\mathcal E$ has every small wide equalizer: these are particular small limits (including the empty family of parallel arrows). Apply [lem-coef-weakly-initial-wide-equalizers] to its weakly initial object $T$ from Step 8. The resulting initial object of $\operatorname{Cocone}(D)$ is exactly a colimit cocone by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: its unique arrow to a cocone $(M,v)$ is the unique vertex map commuting with every leg. Since $D$ was any small diagram, $\mathcal A$ is cocomplete.

source.place: Agent proof, complete implies cocomplete: Freyd initial-object theorem, Mathlib WeaklyInitial.lean:46-66, applied in the category of cocones.

proof.text: Conversely assume $\mathcal A$ accessible and cocomplete. Choose an accessibility cardinal $\kappa$ and a small family of $\kappa$-presentable generators, and let $\mathcal P$ be the small category with these indexed objects and all their $\mathcal A$-morphisms. Repeated representatives cause no difficulty. Put $N(X)(P)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(P,X)$; precomposition defines a presheaf on $\mathcal P$, and postcomposition defines $N:\mathcal A\to[\mathcal P^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Set}_{\mathcal U}]$. This functor is fully faithful. To see fullness, given $\tau:NX\to NY$, present $X=\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}P_i$ with $I$ small $\kappa$-filtered and structure maps $x_i:P_i\to X$. Naturality makes $\tau_{P_i}(x_i)$ a cocone to $Y$, so it induces $f:X\to Y$. For any $g:P\to X$ with $P\in\mathcal P$, presentability gives $g=x_i h$ for some $h:P\to P_i$: presentability identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(P,X)$ with $\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}(P,P_i)$. For sets, the latter colimit is the quotient of the disjoint union of the sets $\operatorname{Hom}(P,P_i)$ by the equivalence relation generated by transition pairs. Compatible maps out of this quotient are exactly compatible maps out of the summands, which checks its colimit property. Each quotient element therefore has a representative $h:P\to P_i$, whose image is $x_i h$. Hence $fg=\tau_{P_i}(x_i)h=\tau_P(g)$ by naturality. Thus $N(f)=\tau$. If $N(f)=N(f')$, then $fx_i=f'x_i$ for every $i$, so $f=f'$ by the colimit property, proving faithfulness.

source.place: Agent proof, cocomplete implies complete: restricted Yoneda is fully faithful, proved explicitly from filtered presentations and presentability, not invoked as an uncited density theorem.

proof.text: For a presheaf $Q:\mathcal P^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Set}_{\mathcal U}$, define its category of elements to have objects $(P,q)$ with $q\in Q(P)$, and arrows $(P,q)\to(P',q')$ the $h:P\to P'$ for which $Q(h)(q')=q$. This category is small: its objects form a small disjoint union of small sets and its arrows form a subset of a small disjoint union of Hom sets. The diagram $(P,q)\mapsto P$ therefore has a colimit $LQ$ in $\mathcal A$ by cocompleteness, with maps $\iota_{P,q}:P\to LQ$.

source.place: Agent proof, cocomplete implies complete: small category-of-elements realization; no colimit over a large index category is used.

proof.text: The colimit property identifies an arrow $LQ\to X$ with maps $v_{P,q}:P\to X$ satisfying $v_{P,q}=v_{P',q'}h$ whenever $Q(h)(q')=q$. These are exactly natural transformations $Q\to NX$: the component at $P$ sends $q$ to $v_{P,q}$, and the stated compatibility is exactly naturality for $h$. Conversely a natural transformation gives these maps and hence a unique arrow $LQ\to X$. A presheaf map $Q\to Q'$ sends $(P,q)$ to $(P,q')$ with $q'$ its image, and the colimit property gives $LQ\to LQ'$; uniqueness gives identities and composition. The displayed bijections are natural in $Q$ and $X$ because both actions compose the same maps $v_{P,q}$. Therefore $L\dashv N$.

source.place: Agent proof, cocomplete implies complete: the adjunction is constructed from its natural Hom bijections, rather than assumed from a representability theorem.

proof.text: The presheaf category in Step 10 is locally small and complete. The natural transformations between two presheaves form a subset of the small product of all component function sets. For a small diagram $(Q_k)$ define its limit at $P$ to be the set of tuples $(q_k)_k\in\prod_k Q_k(P)$ satisfying every diagram equation; this is a small set, with the empty diagram giving the singleton. Restrictions act componentwise and preserve these equations. For any cone of presheaves, the unique componentwise maps into these tuple sets commute with restriction, and so give the unique map of presheaves into the limit. This proves the universal property for all small diagrams.

source.place: Agent proof, cocomplete implies complete: explicit pointwise limits of small-set-valued presheaves.

proof.text: Steps 10 and 12 exhibit $N$ as a fully faithful right adjoint, and Step 13 proves its target complete in the same small universe. Apply [lem-coef-reflective-subcategory-limits] with $R=N$ and its left adjoint $L$ to conclude that $\mathcal A$ is complete. Together with Step 9 and the definitional equivalence of Step 1, this proves all three conditions equivalent.

source.place: Agent proof, cocomplete implies complete: Mathlib Monad/Limits.lean:348-350, reflective completeness, and the final logical assembly.
